articles.title: Need for removal of flexible intramedullary nails used to treat femoral shaft fractures in children: an observational study of 55 children with a minimum of 5-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Nietosvaara NR, Kosola J, Nietosvaara Y, Puhakka J, Helenius I, Laaksonen T
articles.population: Children aged 3-14 years with femoral shaft fractures treated with flexible intramedullary nails
articles.sample_size: 55 children
articles.outcomes: Frequency and timing of nail removal, comparison of removal rates between correctly placed nails and nails that were too long
articles.take_home: About two-thirds of children needed their flexible intramedullary nails removed, usually around 2.4 years after surgery due to pain. Nails that were inserted too long (at or below the growth plate) were much more likely to need removal than correctly placed nails.

articles.title: Traumaplasty for acetabular fractures: Factors associated with additional fracture fixation.
articles.authors: Halvachizadeh S, Bell L, Starr AJ, Rudiger HA, Hax J, Berk T, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing hip replacement for acetabular fractures, including periprosthetic or peri-implant injuries
articles.sample_size: 29 patients (16 receiving additional fracture fixation, 13 without)
articles.outcomes: Association between fracture displacement, Paprosky grade and decision to add separate fracture fixation alongside hip replacement
articles.take_home: Larger gaps in the hip socket fracture were linked to surgeons adding extra fixation during hip replacement surgery, but the study was too small to establish a clear threshold for when fixation is definitely needed.

articles.title: Surgical versus non-surgical treatment for metacarpal shaft fractures : a prospective feasibility study.
articles.authors: Taha R, Leighton P, Davis T, Montgomery A, Karantana A, Murray A, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective multicentre feasibility study with embedded qualitative research
articles.population: Adults aged 16 years and over with acute displaced metacarpal shaft fractures
articles.sample_size: 201 eligible patients, 108 recruited (68% male, median age 32 years)
articles.outcomes: Grip strength, range of motion, radiological parameters, QuickDASH, PROMIS-UE, EQ-5D-5L, and Global Rating of Change measured at six weeks, three months, and six months
articles.take_home: A large randomised trial comparing surgery and non-surgery for broken finger bones appears possible, with good recruitment but retention drops after six weeks. Researchers identified the best questionnaires to use and found participants were happy with the study methods.

articles.title: Patient, surgeon, and institutional variation in implant selection at first-time aseptic revision knee arthroplasty: a registry-based study from the National Joint Registry for England, Wales, Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man, and the Channel Islands.
articles.authors: Tyas B, Hewitt C, Deehan D, Baker P
articles.population: Patients undergoing first-time aseptic revision knee replacement in England, Wales, Northern Ireland, Isle of Man, Guernsey, and Jersey
articles.sample_size: 12,950 patients across 1,250 surgeons and 402 institutions
articles.outcomes: Use of metaphyseal fixation devices, hinged constructs, intramedullary stem fixation, and mobile-bearing implants
articles.take_home: The choice of implant type for revision knee replacements has changed significantly over time and varies considerably between surgeons and hospitals, even after accounting for patient and surgeon factors. High-volume surgeons were more likely to use newer fixation devices, but most of the variation in implant selection cannot be explained by current evidence, suggesting the need for clearer guidance to standardise practice.

articles.title: Computed Tomography Scan Zone-of-Injury Modeling Predicts Need for Definitive Soft-Tissue Coverage and Complications in Open OTA 42A-C Tibial Shaft Fractures.
articles.authors: Vu NH, Esper GW, Goldstein AR, Ganta A, Barrera J, Hacquebord J, et al.
articles.population: Patients with open tibial shaft fractures (OTA 42A-C) treated surgically with preoperative CT imaging and at least 6 months follow-up
articles.sample_size: 122 patients
articles.outcomes: Need for soft-tissue coverage (skin graft, flap, or amputation); soft-tissue and fracture-related complications including nonunion, infection, and coverage failure
articles.take_home: A CT scan measurement model that looks at air gaps, wound size and location was better at predicting which patients would need soft-tissue coverage than the standard Gustilo-Anderson classification system. Patients identified as higher risk had more complications like delayed healing and infection.

articles.title: What matters more in the time to flap: injury-to-flap or definitive-fixation-to-flap?
articles.authors: Mundy LR, Coto SD, O'Hara NN, Wolinsky P, Obremskey WT, Potter BK, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective secondary analysis of data from two prospective randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and older with open fractures requiring acute flap coverage, who underwent definitive fixation and debridement within 72 hours of injury
articles.sample_size: 138 patients (32 with infection, 106 without)
articles.outcomes: Infection rate at 3 months using CDC criteria; time intervals from injury-to-flap, first debridement-to-flap, and definitive fixation-to-flap
articles.take_home: Getting flap surgery within 7 days of the initial injury or first debridement was linked to lower infection rates. However, the timing between fixation surgery and flap surgery did not appear to affect infection risk.

articles.title: Antibiotic Nails Outperform Implant Retention in Preventing Recurrent Infections After Intramedullary Nail Fixation of Tibial Shaft Fractures Complicated by Infection.
articles.authors: Wilhelm ZC, Kommu K, Adler EM, Schermerhorn JT, Arave MD, O'Hara NN, et al.
articles.population: Adults with tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nail fixation who developed deep surgical site infections
articles.sample_size: 96 patients (75 treated with antibiotic nail, 21 with implant retention)
articles.outcomes: 2-year infection recurrence rates requiring reoperation and antibiotics; amputation rate, mortality rate, hospital days, time to recurrence, and number of surgeries after recurrence
articles.take_home: Conversion to an antibiotic-coated nail reduced infection recurrence at 2 years (33% versus 54% with implant retention). However, infection recurrence remains a significant challenge with both approaches, affecting about one in three patients with antibiotic nails and over half of those with implant retention.

articles.title: Unplanned Reoperation and Patient-Reported Outcomes After Operative Treatment of Intraarticular Glenoid Fractures.
articles.authors: McGlone PJ, Funk K, Ambrose M, Chiu A, Gruver-Williams A, Wise A, et al.
articles.population: Adults with operatively managed intraarticular glenoid fractures
articles.sample_size: 54 patients (26 completed long-term outcome assessment)
articles.outcomes: Unplanned reoperation rate and SANE score (shoulder function and satisfaction, 0-100 scale)
articles.take_home: About 28% of patients needed further surgery after their initial operation for a glenoid fracture. Among those assessed years later, most reported excellent shoulder function and satisfaction with a median score of 98 out of 100.

articles.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Prophylactic Inferior Vena Cava Filters in High-Risk Hip Fracture Patients: Clinical implications of an early retrieval strategy.
articles.authors: Kim CH, La CW, Kim JW
articles.population: Patients aged over 50 years with low-energy hip fracture who received prophylactic IVC filters before surgery
articles.sample_size: 156 patients in prophylactic IVC filter group; 4,568 in overall hip fracture cohort
articles.outcomes: Primary: rate of newly developed symptomatic pulmonary thromboembolism. Secondary: IVC filter-related complications, retrieval rates, and 30-day mortality.
articles.take_home: In carefully selected high-risk hip fracture patients (those with confirmed deep vein thrombosis or unable to take blood thinners), temporary IVC filters prevented blood clots moving to the lungs and were safe, with no serious mechanical problems and a 30-day death rate similar to patients without filters.

articles.title: Operative Strategies for Treating Tibial Plateau Fractures in Patients Aged 55 Years and Older: A Five-Year Comparison of Acute Total Knee Arthroplasty with Open Reduction and Internal Fixation, Conversion Total Knee Arthroplasty, and Total Knee Arthroplasty for Osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Wahid M, Bellamy J, Hoskins W, Zaidi Z, Gusho C, Scott CEH, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients aged 55 years and older with tibial plateau fracture, treated between 2005 and 2020
articles.sample_size: 1,321 patients per matched cohort in primary analysis
articles.outcomes: 5-year revision surgery rates, periprosthetic joint infection, surgical site infection, return to operating room, aseptic loosening, manipulation under anesthesia, and periprosthetic fracture
articles.take_home: In older patients with tibial plateau fractures, immediate knee replacement had higher rates of revision surgery and infection compared to fixing the fracture with surgery alone. Immediate knee replacement should generally be reserved for patients most likely to fail with fracture repair.

articles.title: A Novel Technique to Maintain Skeletal Traction During CT Imaging for Acetabular Fractures with Mechanical Instability.
articles.authors: Champagne AA, Cabell GH, Parsons AW, Harman EJ, Torrey JS, Pean CA, et al.
articles.study_type: Technical report with retrospective case series
articles.population: Patients with acetabular fracture dislocations and mechanical instability
articles.sample_size: 15 patients
articles.outcomes: No dislocation episodes during serial CT imaging prior to surgery
articles.take_home: A new low-cost traction method using a ratchet strap and digital scale safely maintained skeletal traction during CT scans of unstable acetabular fractures without causing re-dislocation.

articles.title: The Illusion of Scale: Divergent Orthopaedic Trauma Outcomes Across Large Healthcare Databases.
articles.authors: Croen BJ, Zhuang T, Jagiella-Lodise O, Soma S, Dehghani B, Donegan D, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study comparing two national databases
articles.population: Adult patients aged 18 years and over who had surgery for proximal femur fracture, femoral shaft intramedullary nail, or tibial shaft intramedullary nail between 2015 and 2020
articles.sample_size: 152,340 patients in TriNetX database and 137,326 patients in PearlDiver database
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications at 30, 60 and 90 days including surgical site infection, transfusion, anemia, acute kidney injury, urinary tract infection, pneumonia, wound dehiscence and pulmonary embolism
articles.take_home: The two major databases used for orthopaedic trauma research reported significantly different complication rates for the same procedures, with TriNetX showing higher rates of blood clots in the lungs but lower rates of pneumonia and urinary tract infections. This suggests that researchers need to be cautious when comparing results between different databases as the differences may reflect how each database records information rather than true differences in patient outcomes.

articles.title: Menopausal Hormone Therapy History is Associated with Improved Postoperative Ambulatory Recovery in Postmenopausal Women with Hip Fragility Fractures.
articles.authors: Fox BQ, Kocher SD, Brown C, Olexa M, Ford A, Wittstein J, et al.
articles.population: Postmenopausal women aged 50 and over who had surgery for hip fragility fractures
articles.sample_size: 358 patients (80 with history of menopausal hormone therapy, 278 without)
articles.outcomes: Primary outcomes: ambulatory status and return to baseline ambulation at 30 and 90 days after surgery. Secondary outcomes: hospital readmission at 30 and 90 days, and six-month mortality
articles.take_home: Women with a history of menopausal hormone therapy were more likely to return to their baseline walking ability by 90 days after hip fracture surgery and had fewer readmissions within 30 days. This suggests that prior hormone therapy may help with recovery after hip fracture.

articles.title: Beyond sacral slope change: a new lumbar flexion-based hip-spine classification for total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Shafiei SH, Bromwich L, Plaskos C, Bare J, McMahon S, Carr A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 1,795 primary THA cases in 1,673 patients, mean age 66.1 years
articles.outcomes: Dislocation rates, Hip User Index scores, spinopelvic risk factor prevalence, comparison of classification systems
articles.take_home: A new classification system based on actual lumbar flexion measurements better identifies patients at risk of hip dislocation after hip replacement surgery than the current method based on sacral slope change. This more accurate approach may help surgeons plan operations more individually and reduce complications.

articles.title: Evolving Management of Hip Fracture Patients on Anticoagulant and Antiplatelet Medications: A 22-Year Cohort Study.
articles.authors: House HE, Schwartz A, Shimizu M, Hong I, Cohen JB, Summers HD, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 55 years or older with hip fractures receiving anticoagulant and/or antiplatelet therapy
articles.sample_size: 476 patients (mean age 81.2 years, 60.4% female)
articles.outcomes: Time to surgery, perioperative transfusion, 90-day complications, 90-day mortality, and 1-year readmission
articles.take_home: The type of blood-thinning medication patients were taking did not affect how quickly they had surgery, their 90-day complication rates, or their mortality after hip fracture surgery. Over the 22-year study period, the need for blood transfusions and readmission rates both improved, suggesting that surgical care got better over time regardless of which blood-thinning medication was used.

articles.title: Open reduction of the femoral butterfly fragment in closed femoral shaft fractures is associated with a higher rate of reoperation to promote union: a retrospective clinical cohort.
articles.authors: Schlauch AM, Zakusylo A, Ball G, Biedermann B, Onafowokan O, Kennerly V, et al.
articles.population: Patients with closed femoral shaft fractures treated surgically at a Level I Trauma Center
articles.sample_size: 139 patients (99 without butterfly fragment, 40 with butterfly fragment)
articles.outcomes: Reoperation to promote union, fracture-related infection, and post-operative cortical step sign
articles.take_home: Patients with a butterfly fragment in their femur fracture who had surgery to open up and reduce the fragment had a much higher rate of needing further surgery (67% versus 7%), suggesting that leaving the fragment alone without opening it up may be better for healing.

articles.title: Association Between Baseline Anemia and Nonunion After Proximal Humerus Fracture Across the Adult Lifespan.
articles.authors: Nakken ER, Mamonov A, Garcia-Canga B, Whitney DG, Lang A, Aibinder WR
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using administrative claims data
articles.population: Adults aged 19 years and over who sustained a proximal humerus fracture
articles.sample_size: 25,109 adults with anemia and 64,389 without anemia
articles.outcomes: Incidence of nonunion of proximal humerus fracture from 6 to 18 months post-fracture
articles.take_home: Anemia before a proximal humerus fracture was linked to a higher risk of the bone not healing properly, but mainly in younger and middle-aged adults (aged 40 to 60 years). This association was not seen in older adults aged 70 and over.

articles.title: Exposure technology and tissue protection in anterior and anterolateral thoracic/thoracolumbar fracture surgery: An international surgeon survey of retractor performance, mitigation strategies, and design priorities.
articles.authors: Lewandrowski KU, Liodakis E, Fritz T, Burkhardt B, Oertel J, Sprengel K, et al.
articles.population: Surgeons performing anterior and anterolateral thoracic and thoracolumbar fracture surgery
articles.sample_size: 82 surgeons from 22 countries (39 with personal experience of the procedures)
articles.outcomes: Retractor performance, tissue-protection strategies, design priorities, and complication rates
articles.take_home: Surgeons use various retractors for spine fracture surgery and report that large body size, difficulty seeing the area, and protecting nerves and blood vessels are key challenges. Future retractors should focus on better blade design, lighting, and imaging features to improve safety.

articles.title: Lower serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels are associated with greater fracture complexity in adult orthopaedic trauma patients: an OTA/AO classification-based cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Barros Castro AX, Barros Prieto E, Ballesteros Ponce C, Noboa Freile CE, Penaherrera C, Endara F
articles.population: Adult orthopaedic trauma patients at tertiary hospitals in Quito, Ecuador
articles.sample_size: 126 adults with fractures and available vitamin D measurements
articles.outcomes: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and fracture complexity using OTA/AO classification
articles.take_home: Patients with more complex fractures tended to have lower vitamin D levels. For each 1 ng/mL increase in vitamin D, the odds of having a more complex fracture decreased, though this was an observational association and does not prove vitamin D deficiency causes complex fractures.

articles.title: Early deep infection after operatively managed low-velocity tibial gunshot fractures is associated with older age, temporary external fixation, and longer time to definitive fixation.
articles.authors: Boutany M, Abdelnour D, Jandali D, Tobia J, Elmenini H, Nasr K, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients with operatively managed tibial fractures from low-velocity gunshot wounds
articles.sample_size: 113 patients with 116 tibial fractures
articles.outcomes: Deep infection (requiring operative debridement, intravenous antibiotics, or positive cultures) occurred in 11.2% of patients. Older age, temporary external fixation, and longer time from injury to definitive fixation were associated with increased infection risk.
articles.take_home: Among gunshot wound fractures of the shin bone treated with surgery and antibiotics, about 1 in 10 patients developed a deep infection. The risk was higher in older patients and when temporary external fixation was used before the final operation, particularly if the definitive surgery was delayed.

articles.title: Perioperative antiplatelet use is not associated with increased risk of mortality among older adults undergoing operative hip fracture repair.
articles.authors: Akodu M, Rajesh D, Steele A, Aung N, Zhang C, McTague M, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 65 years and older undergoing surgical fixation for hip fractures
articles.sample_size: 965 patients
articles.outcomes: Mortality at 30, 90 and 365 days; length of stay over 7 days; blood transfusion need; 30-day readmission
articles.take_home: Continuing antiplatelet medications during hip fracture surgery does not increase the risk of death in older adults. However, patients on these medications may have higher rates of needing blood transfusions and being readmitted to hospital within 30 days.

articles.title: After-hours hip fracture surgery-influence on reoperation risk, mortality, and surgical complications: a cohort study of 98,607 patients from the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register.
articles.authors: Boutera AT, Dybvik E, Engesaeter LB, Guy P, Kristensen TB, Leer-Salvesen S, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years and older with hip fracture
articles.sample_size: 98,607 patients from the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register (2005-2023)
articles.outcomes: 1-year reoperation risk, 30-day mortality, and intraoperative complications, comparing surgery performed during daytime (08:00-16:00), evening (16:00-22:00), and nighttime (22:00-08:00)
articles.take_home: Hip fracture surgery performed outside regular working hours was not associated with higher rates of needing further surgery within a year, death within 30 days, or surgical complications compared with daytime surgery. Nighttime surgery was actually associated with slightly lower 30-day mortality.

articles.title: Additional FiberTape-Cerclage(R) augmentation or "Bumper-plate" osteosynthesis for symphyseal arthrodesis - A biomechanical study.
articles.authors: Fritz T, Kessler J, Orth M, Pohlemann T, Pizanis A, Norrick S, et al.
articles.population: Synthetic pelvic models
articles.sample_size: 24 models (8 per group)
articles.outcomes: Compression force resistance, contact area preservation, stability under cyclic loading in unilateral and bilateral stance
articles.take_home: Adding FiberTape cerclage to a single plate provided 49% better resistance to separation forces compared to a single plate alone, and worked as well as using two plates whilst allowing better X-ray visibility of healing. This was a laboratory study using artificial pelves, not actual patients.

articles.title: Field Amputation by helicopter emergency service personnel: A cross-sectional survey of clinical practice and experience within air ambulance services in England.
articles.authors: Dunkerley W, Wilkinson J
articles.population: Helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) in England
articles.sample_size: 14 HEMS services
articles.outcomes: Current field amputation clinical guidance, practice, equipment, training, governance and incidence of field amputations
articles.take_home: All 14 English air ambulance services surveyed can perform emergency amputations if needed, though there is little standardisation between them. Only 4 services had actually carried out amputations in the past five years, totalling 6 cases.

articles.title: The epidemiology and burden of injury in The Gambia: A prospective trauma registry study.
articles.authors: Njai A, Zeitoun S, Njie M, Kah M, Secka A, Agarwal-Harding KJ, et al.
articles.population: Injured patients presenting to a hospital trauma unit in The Gambia
articles.sample_size: 3380 patients enrolled from June 2022 to September 2025
articles.outcomes: Patient demographics, injury mechanisms, anatomic location of injuries, injury types, and emergency unit disposition
articles.take_home: Most injuries in The Gambia occurred in young males from transport accidents on streets and highways, with lower limbs, head and hands most commonly affected. The study found that over half of patients were sent home, but many left before completing treatment, highlighting the need for better road safety, improved emergency services, and expanded trauma care facilities.

articles.title: Retrograde gearshift pedicle probe-assisted reduction of displaced superior pubic rami fractures: A technical note.
articles.authors: Hellwinkel JE, van Jaarsveld JL, Duldner JE, Paya AM, Aslanturk O, Mauffrey CP, et al.
articles.population: Patients with displaced superior pubic rami fractures
articles.outcomes: Successful fracture reduction, safe wire or screw insertion, no complications, restoration of superior pubic ramus corridor
articles.take_home: A curved probe inserted backwards can help surgeons straighten and reposition broken pubic bones, making it safer to place metal fixation devices. All three fractures in this small study were successfully treated without problems.

articles.title: Does CT seatbelt sign, traumatic abdominal wall hernia or body habitus predict injuries and patient outcomes following a restrained motor vehicle collision? A New Zealand cohort study.
articles.authors: Rouse D, Shekkeris A, Lauchlan R, McCombie A
articles.population: Major trauma patients (injury severity score ≥12) restrained by seatbelt in motor vehicle collisions at Christchurch Hospital
articles.sample_size: 316 patients
articles.outcomes: Organ injury rates and grades, death rates, injury severity score, number of operating sessions, length of ICU stay, hospital stay
articles.take_home: Patients with a CT seatbelt sign or traumatic abdominal wall hernia had higher rates of internal organ injury and worse outcomes including longer hospital stays and more operations needed. Body fat distribution did not significantly affect outcomes in seatbelt-restrained motor vehicle collisions.

articles.title: History of operative pelvic ring fixation is associated with increased risk of cesarean delivery: A matched retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Scott J, Bukowinski AT, Lutgendorf MA, Romano CJ, Hall C, Gumbs GR, et al.
articles.population: Women of childbearing age with and without history of operative pelvic ring fixation who had live births
articles.sample_size: 79 women with pelvic fixation history and 790 matched controls
articles.outcomes: Caesarean delivery rates and indications for caesarean delivery
articles.take_home: Women with a history of pelvic fixation surgery were twice as likely to have a caesarean delivery compared to women without pelvic injury, though nearly half still delivered vaginally. The study suggests that pelvic fixation alone should not automatically mean caesarean delivery is necessary, and each woman needs individualised assessment.

articles.title: Concomitant pelvic ring injury compromises acetabular reduction quality: A propensity score-matched analysis with surgical sequence subgroup study.
articles.authors: Lee CY, Jung WC, Lee JH, Yoon TR, Park KS
articles.population: Patients with acetabular fractures, with and without concomitant pelvic ring injury, treated at a tertiary trauma centre between 2004 and 2023
articles.sample_size: 40 matched patients (20 with isolated acetabular fractures, 20 with combined pelvic ring and acetabular injuries)
articles.outcomes: Primary: anatomical acetabular reduction (modified Matta criteria). Secondary: pelvic ring reduction and postoperative complications including post-traumatic osteoarthritis
articles.take_home: Patients with both pelvic ring and acetabular fractures are significantly less likely to achieve good acetabular reduction compared to those with acetabular fractures alone. Fixing the acetabulum first showed a trend towards better reduction, and was associated with fewer complications like arthritis, though the evidence is limited.

articles.title: Optimizing success in scalp replantation for total scalp avulsion injuries: A systematic review and case series.
articles.authors: Datta S, Hanna SA, Haxho F, Lipa JE, Snell LJ
articles.population: Adults aged 16 years and over with total, near-total, or at least 70% scalp avulsion injuries
articles.sample_size: 162 cases from 70 studies (plus 2 additional cases from authors' trauma centre)
articles.outcomes: Complete scalp survival of 90% or more achieved in 64.2% of cases. Average 1.8 arterial and 2.5 venous anastomoses performed. Superficial temporal vessels were most commonly used.
articles.take_home: Microsurgical replantation is the standard treatment for total scalp avulsion, with over 60% of patients achieving excellent scalp survival. Using multiple venous connections and prioritising superficial temporal blood vessels, along with close monitoring and anticoagulation after surgery, gives the best chance of success.

articles.title: Nonoperative Management Deserves Consideration for Select Patients with Valgus-Impacted Femoral Neck Fractures.
articles.authors: Bishop JA, Goodnough LH
articles.study_type: Review and synthesis of randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses
articles.population: Patients with valgus-impacted femoral neck fractures
articles.outcomes: Rates of uneventful healing, need for reoperation, implant-related complications, mortality, morbidity after delayed arthroplasty
articles.take_home: For carefully selected patients who are mentally alert, independent, medically stable and able to protect their weight-bearing, nonoperative treatment can achieve healing rates similar to surgery without higher risk if conversion to joint replacement becomes necessary later. Close monitoring is needed to detect problems early.
